messages:
maria: Heads-up — during peak yesterday EUW2 node group 12 had sustained GPU memory >95% for ~18m, autoscaler started throttling new pods. Several requests experienced 5-10s added latency. Not a full OOM but a near-miss. Opening this thread to capture findings, timeline, and follow-ups.

aj: Saw alerts at ~17:12 UTC. Grafana dashboards (link: https://grafana.redwood/euw2/group12?from=169) show repeated memory spikes and eviction events. Will attach a cropped graph.

sasha: Root cause looks like two things aligning: long-chat KV cache retention (we had larger-than-usual prefixes) + a nightly eval job (eval-runner) that accidentally ramped sequence length for a subset of requests. That evicted caches unevenly and caused memory churn.

kevin: Quick numbers: 6/24 nodes in the pool hit >90% memory; estimated extra GPU-minutes ~4,200 during the incident window. Cost delta rough estimate ~$600 for the 18m sustained period.

devin: Relevant log snippet from infer-rt-12 around the spike: ```2028-11-16T17:12:01Z infer-rt-12 kernel: GPU memory high: 97% kv_cache.evicted=1 pid=4321```

maria: Immediate action items I propose: 1) tighten autoscaler memory threshold from 92%->88% for node-group 12 as a temporary mitigation; 2) fix affinity/taint for eval-runner so it lands in a spot pool; 3) add sustained-memory alert (memory>90% for >10m) to avoid blind 15m windows; 4) add short-term buffer to EUW2 capacity during promos.

lucy: Note: eval-runner was misconfigured to request dedicated GPUs (should be spot). Ticket created: INF-4237 (eval-runner affinity fix).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INF-4237 — gpu-near-saturation-euw2 — assignee: sasha — priority: P2

aj: Postmortem detail — the eval fixture bumped seq_len in a test suite from 1024->4096. That multiplier blew up KV usage because some requests kept long histories. We need guardrails to reject large seq_len changes in CI that run on prod-like clusters.

sasha: Mitigation steps we ran: manual prefix cache eviction on 4 nodes + rolling restart of 2 pods on the most impacted hosts. Headroom recovered in ~6 minutes after eviction. No customer-facing errors reported besides latency.

kevin: Long-term proposals: (a) per-tenant soft-limits on KV cache size; (b) smarter eviction policy that favors long-tail sessions; (c) reserve 6% node memory for autoscaler headroom (configurable per node-group); (d) add a simulated burst test in staging for seq_len regression.

maria: Short timeline to include in the retro doc: 17:07 — small memory fluctuation alerts start; 17:12 — sustained >95% on 6 nodes, autoscaler throttles; 17:20 — manual eviction + targeted restarts; 17:26 — metrics return to normal; 17:30 — post-incident checks complete.

devin: Can capacity-planning update the EUW2 forecast with a 15% promotional buffer for the next quarter? This incident shows we have little runway during modest spikes. Tagging capacity-planning and infra-sre.

lucy: I'll update the forecast sheet and add the buffer. Also scheduling a dedicated chaos/eviction test to validate our eviction and autoscaler thresholds.

maria: Thanks all — I'll collate notes, link dashboards and logs into the INF-4237 ticket and propose changes for the weekly oncall sync. Aim to close follow-ups in 48h. :thumbsup:
